key_facts: SQL is a standard computer language for relational database management and data manipulation.

SQL is divided into three sub-languages: DDL (Data Definition Language with CREATE/ALTER/DROP), DML (Data Manipulation Language with SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE), and DCL (Data Control Language with COMMIT/ROLLBACK/GRANT/REVOKE).
A schema in SQL is a group of tables and other constructs that belong to the same database application, created via 'CREATE SCHEMA Schema_Name AUTHORIZATION Authorization_Identifier'.
A catalog in SQL is a named collection of schemas.
CREATE TABLE supports column constraints (NOT NULL, UNIQUE, PRIMARY KEY, DEFAULT, CHECK) and table-level constraints including FOREIGN KEY with referential actions ON UPDATE and ON DELETE.
generated_text: Introduction to Structured Query Language (SQL) Structured Query Language (SQL) is a standard computer language for relational database management and data manipulation. SQL commands can be broadly categorized into three basic types, each serving a distinct purpose in interacting with a database. Data Definition Language (DDL) : Used to define and manage the structure of database objects. Data Manipulation Language (DML) : Used to retrieve, add, modify, and delete data within database objects. Data Control Language (DCL) : Used to manage user access and permissions to the data. Data Definition Language (DDL) DDL permits the specification of data types, structures, and any data constraints. These specifications are stored in the database itself. The primary DDL commands are CREATE, ALTER, and DROP. CREATE The CREATE command is used to make a new database object, such as a database, table, index, or user. ALTER The ALTER command is used to change the definition of a base table or other schema elements. This includes actions like adding or dropping a column, changing a column definition, or modifying constraints. -- Example: Adding a new column to the Employee table ALTER TABLE Employee ADD Job VARCHAR(15); -- Example: Dropping a column from the Employee table ALTER TABLE Employee DROP COLUMN Address CASCADE; DROP The DROP command is used to remove an entire database object. When an object like a table is dropped, options such as CASCADE can be used to ensure that all constraints and views that reference the table are also dropped automatically from the schema. Data Manipulation Language (DML) DML commands are used to manage the data stored within the database tables. It's important to note that an SQL table is a multi-set (or bag) of tuples, meaning it can have two or more rows that are identical in all their attribute values. SELECT The SELECT command is used to retrieve information from a database. It is the primary tool for querying data and consists of several clauses to refine the results: SELECT : Specifies which columns are to appear in the output. FROM : Specifies the table(s) to be used. WHERE : Filters rows based on a condition. GROUP BY : Forms groups of rows with the same column value. HAVING : Filters groups subject to some condition. ORDER BY : Specifies the order of the output. INSERT The INSERT command is used to add one or more tuples (rows) to a relation (table). The attribute values should be listed in the same order as the attributes were specified in the CREATE TABLE command, unless the attribute names are explicitly listed. INSERT INTO TableName (Attribute1, Attribute2, …) VALUES (value1, value2, …); UPDATE The UPDATE command is used to modify the attribute values of one or more selected tuples in a table. UPDATE TableName SET Set-Clause WHERE Condition; DELETE The DELETE command removes tuples from a relation. If the WHERE clause is omitted, all tuples in the relation are deleted, leaving an empty table. Tuples are deleted from only one table at a time unless referential integrity constraints with CASCADE are specified. DELETE FROM TableName WHERE Condition; Data Control Language (DCL) DCL commands are used to control access to data within the database. They are based on three central concepts: users, database objects, and privileges (e.g., SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE). GRANT The GRANT command is used to pass privileges on database objects to other users. GRANT <privilege list> ON <database objects> TO <user list>; REVOKE The REVOKE command is used to take back or cancel privileges that were previously granted to other users. REVOKE <privilege list> ON <database objects> FROM <user list>; Summary This lesson provided an overview of the fundamental categories of Structured Query Language: DDL : Commands like CREATE , ALTER , and DROP are used to define the database schema. DML : Commands like SELECT , INSERT , UPDATE , and DELETE are used to query and modify the data itself. DCL : Commands like GRANT and REVOKE are used to manage data access and user permissions.
